ISYS 490 · Transformers, hands-on

Inside GPT-2

Pick a sentence and follow it through the five steps a transformer uses to choose the next word. Every number on this page comes from the real GPT-2 model.

Click a word to select it for steps 2 and 3.
1

Tokenization

The text is split into tokens, and each token gets an ID number from the model’s vocabulary.

This sentence

Try your own text

A faint · marks a space that belongs to the token. Tokens are also how LLM use is billed: you pay per token sent and received. Every model family has its own vocabulary, so the IDs here (GPT-2) differ from the ones on the slide, which come from a newer OpenAI tokenizer.

2

Embedding + positional encoding

Each token becomes a list of numbers that carries its meaning. A second list says where it sits in the sentence. The two are added together.

below 0above 0· hover a square to see its value

You are seeing 16 of the 768 numbers GPT-2 uses for every token. GPT-2 learns its position numbers during training instead of building them from sine and cosine waves. Try a word that appears twice, like “a” in the snack sentence: same meaning numbers, different position numbers.

3

Attention, with masking

The selected word looks back at the words before it and decides how much each one matters. Words after it are masked: it cannot see them.

Show attention for every word at once

Each row is a word doing the looking; each column is a word being looked at. Darker means more attention. The striped triangle is the masking: no word can look ahead.

4

Feedforward → softmax: the next word

The model scores every one of its 50,257 tokens. Softmax turns the scores into probabilities that add up to 100%. Here are the top 10.

1.0
0.20.50.81.01.31.62.0

Low temperature makes the top word even more likely, so the model plays it safe. High temperature evens out the probabilities, so less likely words get picked more often.

5

Generate, one word at a time

Add a word to the sentence and everything above updates for the next one. This is how an LLM writes: one token, then the next.

About this tool

Model and data. All numbers come from GPT-2 small (OpenAI, 2019; 124 million parameters), run ahead of time and stored in this page, so nothing is downloaded and every laptop gets the same results. The model file is the one published with Transformer Explainer.

For each sentence, the three most likely next words can be added, up to 4 words deep. The nurse and engineer sentences are for comparing probabilities only; generation is turned off for them because GPT-2’s news-heavy training data steers those continuations toward crime reporting.

Attention. GPT-2 has 144 attention patterns (12 layers × 12 heads). Step 3 shows one of them, layer 10, head 1, chosen because it clearly links related words (bank → paycheck, bank → river, a → apple). Each sentence is fed to the model after GPT-2’s start-of-text marker, which absorbs much of the attention; the marker is not shown, and the remaining attention is rescaled to 100%.

Probabilities. Step 4 shows real probabilities at seven temperature settings. “Let the model pick” chooses among the three explorable words, weighted by their probabilities at the current temperature.
